events.speaker: Phil
events.cue: The radio clicks on. Tuesday, February 2. Your clean shirt is folded exactly as the hotel left it. Record a voice memo nobody else can hear. It can be for Jo, for tomorrow's you, or for nobody at all. The small bottle of maple syrup is back on the dresser, wrapped and unopened. Choose what you physically do with it. The recorder is running. Before this Tuesday you remember 39 complete days in this run ending before you could reach Wednesday breakfast.

choices.pack: Phil tucks the unopened maple syrup into his travel bag.
choices.leave: Phil leaves the wrapped bottle on the hotel dresser.
choices.open: Phil opens the bottle for himself this morning.
choices.pour_out: Phil empties the bottle into the hotel sink.

events.line: It’s in the bag. Eight o'clock, sharp. Don’t let that foot ruin the pancakes again.
events.effect: Phil tucks the unopened maple syrup into his travel bag.

events.speaker: Phil
events.cue: Rita and Larry wait at the cue sheet. Beside it is the only weather cartridge: your own cheerful voice doing an old forecast, down to a small breath before your first word. At seven, it can substitute for you on air. Do something with it while they can see. They can hear anything you say. Before this Tuesday you remember 39 complete days in this run ending before you could reach Wednesday breakfast.

choices.pocket_cart: Phil pockets the station's only copy of his old weather recording.
choices.mark_archive: Phil writes ARCHIVE across the weather cartridge and leaves it by the cue sheet.
choices.leave_cart: Phil leaves the weather cartridge by the cue sheet, unmarked.

events.line: That is the only copy of me left, Larry, and I am not leaving it in a folder for the next guy to play. The static isn't going anywhere if I let go.
events.effect: Phil pockets the station's only copy of his old weather recording.

events.speaker: Rita
events.cue: You just saw Phil at the cue sheet. Speak to him or to Larry, or let the moment go.

choices.tear_carbon: Rita gives Phil the yellow carbon copy of the cue sheet.
choices.keep_carbon: Rita clips the yellow carbon back under her sheet.

events.line: Hand me that carbon copy before you shred it, Phil. If that tape is the only thing you're taking, I want the sheet so we know what actually went to air tonight.
events.effect: Rita gives Phil the yellow carbon copy of the cue sheet.

events.speaker: Larry
events.cue: You're beside Rita. Phil can hear you. You can answer either one. The crew still has to get the equipment across the street.

choices.take_case: Larry picks up the equipment case.
choices.set_down: Larry sets the equipment case on the floor.

events.line: We are not carrying it across the street, Rita. We are not. The van is idling, right? Let it idling.
events.effect: Larry picks up the equipment case.

events.speaker: Phil
events.cue: The coach door is open. The projection booth across the street has a service door. There is a stairwell at the hotel where the radio can't be heard. Go where you actually want to go. You can speak under your breath. Before this Tuesday you remember 39 complete days in this run ending before you could reach Wednesday breakfast.
events.line:
Eight o'clock, sharp.
I'm done fighting the static.

events.speaker: Alma
events.cue: The door is shut. Only Rita and Larry are with you. You have the key; the last reel has eight minutes left. They can bring a microphone, give you one private line to Nell, or pack up. You have not given permission. Open the conversation however you like.
events.line: Larry, take that mic and put it down. I don't want to hear what you're going to say.

events.speaker: Larry
events.cue: Speak to Alma or Rita. They were not both at the hotel desk. You decide what to repeat, if anything. You have a pencil and an empty reel box.

choices.write_label: Larry turns the reel box over and writes on its blank label.

events.speaker: Rita
events.cue: Alma and Larry are here with you. Their words are still in the room. There is exactly one line at seven. Ask for something you actually need, or refuse what's being asked.

choices.draw_chair: Rita pulls a chair over to Alma.
choices.stay_door: Rita stays by the closed door.

events.line: I need you to pick the piece, Alma, right now. Because if you leave it to me, I'm not doing it.
events.effect: Rita pulls a chair over to Alma.

events.speaker: Alma
events.cue: Answer the people here. You can reserve your voice for Nell, let people hear it publicly as well, or withhold it altogether. Their jobs do not oblige you to help.

choices.family_only: Alma permits only a private call to Nell.
choices.public_too: Alma permits either the public microphone or a private call.

events.line: Put the chair back. I am running the picture, not the schedule.

events.speaker: Larry
events.cue: One last thing you could say to either of them before the reel runs out.

choices.hold_door: Larry holds the door for Alma.

events.line: I’m just watching the dust motes. Don’t need another ghost in the booth.

events.speaker: Phil
events.cue: There is a telephone here. You can ring Jo in Pittsburgh, or let her have the afternoon to herself. If you call, say what she hears when she picks up. If you leave it alone, keep the line empty. Before this Tuesday you remember 39 complete days in this run ending before you could reach Wednesday breakfast.
events.line: Hey. Don't hang up. I'm not bringing a wrench, I'm bringing myself.

events.speaker: Jo
events.cue: Phil is on the telephone. You don't see his surroundings. One couch foot is still stuck. Answer him as you please.

choices.stay: Jo stays on the line for another beat.

events.line: I'm not bringing a wrench, am I? The foot is stuck. I'm making the pancakes tonight.
events.effect: Jo stays on the line for another beat.

events.speaker: Phil
events.cue: A town phone directory gives the regional station's desk number. You can call Rita there, tape something for yourself or stay quiet. If you call, she picks up; your line is the only part heard at the other end. Before this Tuesday you remember 39 complete days in this run ending before you could reach Wednesday breakfast.

choices.call_desk: Rita picks up the station telephone.
choices.memo: Phil keeps this recording to himself.

events.line: You're making pancakes? Good. Eight o'clock, sharp.

events.speaker: Rita
events.cue: The phone is back on its cradle. Larry needs to know what to set up. Tell him what you want, or let him choose. He can still refuse.

choices.clear_space: Rita clears a space beside the patch.
choices.leave_space: Rita keeps her hands in her pockets.

events.line: Larry, pull the case to the left. I'm taking the Rialto piece, and I don't want you deciding what's good.
events.effect: Rita clears a space beside the patch.

events.speaker: Larry
events.cue: You have time to prepare one input. Answer the people in this room. The old recording is usable only if it is here.

choices.set_mic: Larry tests the live microphone for Alma.

events.line: Yeah, you pick. I'm just here to make sure the silence doesn't get charged as airtime.

events.speaker: Rita
events.cue: Seven o'clock. Make the patch or let the slot go. Anything you say is to Larry and Alma inside the control room.

choices.silence: Rita lets the seven o’clock slot pass in silence.

events.effect: Rita lets the seven o’clock slot pass in silence.

events.speaker: Alma
events.cue: The slot is gone. Say what you want Rita and Larry to hear before you take your coat.
events.line: It’s empty on the wire. Go ahead and fill it. I’m done here.

events.speaker: Phil
events.cue: At seven you tuned to the regional frequency. What you heard: The regional frequency carries room tone. You cannot tell why. Now, hours later, the pocket recorder clicks on in your hand. Leave a private voice memo for morning about the part of today you can still hear. Speak as Phil, or play out the silence. Before this Tuesday you remember 39 complete days in this run ending before you could reach Wednesday breakfast.

choices.keep: Phil lets the last recording play to the end.
